 2                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 3   Resolution Number 4305, by Senator Marchione, 

 4   congratulating student-athlete Kevin Huerter 

 5   upon the occasion of being named Mr. New York 

 6   State Basketball by the Basketball Coaches 

 7   Association of New York.

 8                ACTING PRESIDENT AKSHAR:   Senator 

 9   Marchione.

10                SENATOR MARCHIONE:   Thank you, 

11   Mr. President.  I rise for the purpose of 

12   speaking on my legislative resolution.  

13                I've often said that any time we 

14   can showcase the best and brightest of 

15   New York's youth, we should take that 

16   opportunity to do so.  Today represents one of 

17   those opportunities.  

18                It is my privilege to recognize and 

19   congratulate student-athlete Kevin Huerter -- 

20   and if Kevin would stand, please -- a senior on 

21   the Shenendehowa Boys Varsity Basketball Team, 

22   and a resident of my hometown, the Town of 

23   Halfmoon.

24                Kevin Huerter, who is with me today 

25   on the Senate floor, was named Mr. New York 


                                                                2036

 1   State Basketball by the Basketball Coaches 

 2   Association of New York on March 9th.  Being 

 3   named Mr. New York State Basketball is an 

 4   incredible privilege.  In fact, it's New York 

 5   State's highest individual honor in basketball.  

 6                To help illustrate just how big of a 

 7   deal this is, my grandsons actually came to visit 

 8   with me today.  This is Noah and Eli, and they 

 9   love Kevin Huerter.  They follow him in 

10   basketball, and I hear them running around my 

11   home yelling "Kevin Huerter, woo!"

12                (Laughter.)

13                SENATOR MARCHIONE:   They just -- 

14   they just -- they just wanted to be here and to 

15   meet him.  

16                And you know, along with that, with 

17   your honors, though, comes the responsibility of 

18   being a role model to people just like my 

19   grandsons Noah and Eli.  You have displayed 

20   outstanding athletic skill, tremendous 

21   dedication, true sportsmanship, and real 

22   leadership.  

23                During the 2015-2016 season, Kevin 

24   Huerter averaged 22.5 points per game, 

25   8.3 rebounds per game, and 7.2 assists per game.  


                                                                2037

 1   In achieving these impressive milestones, he 

 2   became the second all-time leading scorer for 

 3   Shenendehowa, as well as its all-time assist 

 4   leader and the fourth player in school history to 

 5   surpass the 1,000-point mark.  

 6                A three-year captain, he played for 

 7   four years on the Plainsmen varsity squad and was 

 8   named MVP of the 2015 NYSPHSAA championship team.  

 9                Kevin Huerter is also only the 

10   second Section II or Shenendehowa player to ever 

11   be named Mr. New York State Basketball.

12                As the Daily Gazette noted 

13   previously, past winners of the Mr. New York 

14   State Basketball award included NBA stars such as 

15   Elton Brand, Jamal Mashburn, and Stephon Marbury.  

16   Kevin, you are among some terrific athletic 

17   company.

18                He's known for his exceptional 

19   talent and unselfishness on and off the court.  

20   Kevin Huerter plans on continuing his basketball 

21   career at the University of Maryland.  

22                The athletic talent displayed by him 

23   is due in great part to the efforts of Coach Tony 

24   Dzikas, who has helped Kevin develop into the 

25   player and person that he is today, and also 


                                                                2038

 1   Christopher Culnan, director of athletics and 

 2   physical education for the Shenendehowa Central 

 3   School District.  

 4                Both Coach Dzikas and Mr. Culnan are 

 5   with me today on the Senate floor, and both 

 6   Mr. and Mrs. Huerter are also here today.

 7                Kevin Huerter's high school career 

 8   has been outstanding.  And as my grandsons' 

 9   presence attests to, he is loyally and 

10   enthusiastically supported by my family, friends, 

11   fans and the entire community.

12                Sports instill important lifelong 

13   values -- teamwork, sacrifice, pride and 

14   accomplishment.  Kevin Huerter embodies these 

15   values and has made a genuine contribution to the 

16   spirit of excellence which is a tradition of 

17   Shenendehowa and the Plainsmen.  

18                I ask my colleagues to join me in 

19   recognizing and congratulating Kevin Huerter on 

20   being named Mr. New York State Basketball by the 

21   Basketball Coaches Association of New York.  

22                Congratulations, Kevin.

23                (Applause.)

17                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

18   Resolution Number 4772, by Senator 

19   Stewart-Cousins, memorializing Governor Andrew M. 

20   Cuomo to proclaim April 17-23, 2016, as Abusive 

21   Head Trauma/Shaken Baby Syndrome Awareness Week 

22   in the State of New York.

23                ACTING PRESIDENT AKSHAR:   Senator 

24   Stewart-Cousins.

25                SENATOR STEWART-COUSINS:   Thank 


                                                                2041

 1   you, Mr. President.

 2                I rise today, as I rise annually, to 

 3   just say very simply:  Do not shake your baby.  

 4                Recent statistics in the United 

 5   States show that 679,000 children were victims of 

 6   abuse and neglect in the United States.  And you 

 7   know, we're talking a lot about abuse in many 

 8   areas over this past few weeks.  The statistics 

 9   also include 64,578 children in New York State; 

10   6,482 were under the age of one.

11                The particular thing that I'm 

12   talking about today, though, is shaken baby 

13   syndrome, which is also part of these abuse 

14   statistics.  It's stated that between 1200 and 

15   1400 children annually are diagnosed with AHT or 

16   shaken baby syndrome every year.  

17                And it is simply that; it is someone 

18   who decides, for whatever reason -- usually 

19   because the child is crying -- to shake their 

20   baby.

21                The reason why I stand up annually 

22   to talk about this is because 14 years ago, a 

23   child of 8 months, in the custody of a 

24   babysitter, was killed.  And the babysitter 

25   couldn't figure out what it was that she'd done.  


                                                                2042

 1   And actually, after the autopsy showed the trauma 

 2   to the brain of the child, it got back to the 

 3   fact that the babysitter shook the baby and the 

 4   baby died.

 5                So there has been a mission.  New 

 6   York State has been very clear about making sure 

 7   hospitals give the parents of newborns 

 8   information on shaken baby syndrome.  There has 

 9   been some awareness that's raised.  

10                But every day, some crying child may 

11   disturb the parent to the extent that they think 

12   if they shake this baby, the baby will stop 

13   crying.  The baby will not stop crying because 

14   you shake the baby.  And in more cases than we 

15   want to acknowledge, the baby is damaged.

16                So again, don't shake your baby.  

17   Tell people not to shake the baby.  The baby will 

18   stop crying.  Love your baby, and avoid the 

19   possibility not only of death and trauma, but of 

20   learning disabilities and other complications 

21   from damaging your baby's brain.

22                Thank you.

23                ACTING PRESIDENT AKSHAR:   Thank 

24   you, Senator Stewart-Cousins.
